title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: HAL'S BIG MOUTH
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Hal Dombrowski, a forty-seven-year-old delivery driver from Akron, Ohio.
Hal climbs a hundred porches a day, but rests halfway up his own stairs.
Then, at Thanksgiving, with pie in his mouth, he said five dangerous words. I could run a marathon.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE FORM
segments.quote: The difference between a jogger and a runner is an entry blank.
segments.author: George Sheehan
lines: His daughter Nicole, a marathon runner, slid a paper across the table.
She said the running doctor George Sheehan put it best:
The difference between a jogger and a runner is an entry blank.
Hal wasn't even a jogger. He signed anyway, whipped cream on his thumb.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: FOUR MAILBOXES
segments.quote: All truly great thoughts are conceived by walking.
segments.author: Friedrich Nietzsche
lines: His first run lasted four mailboxes. A basset hound passed him.
Mrs. Abernathy, a retired professor on his route, had a mug from the German thinker Friedrich Nietzsche:
All truly great thoughts are conceived by walking.
So Hal walked. Every night. And his great thought was this: tomorrow, run one more mailbox.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE UGLY FACE
segments.quote: I was not talented enough to run and smile at the same time.
segments.author: Emil Zatopek
lines: By spring he ran two miles, but on back streets. His running face looked like a man stepping on a Lego.
Nicole laughed and told him about Emil Zatopek, a Czech Olympic champion famous for his painful face:
I was not talented enough to run and smile at the same time.
Hal stopped hiding. He ran down Main Street, ugly and happy.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: SIX A.M.
segments.quote: Associate with those who will make a better man of you. Welcome those whom you yourself can improve.
segments.author: Seneca
lines: Then came the summer heat, and Hal started skipping runs.
Mrs. Abernathy handed him a note from Seneca, the old Roman thinker:
Associate with those who will make a better man of you. Welcome those whom you yourself can improve.
So he joined the six a.m. club at the donut shop, mostly grandmas. They pushed his pace. He brought donuts.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: MILE TWENTY
segments.quote: The impediment to action advances action. What stands in the way becomes the way.
segments.author: Marcus Aurelius
lines: Race day. At mile twenty, both calves cramped. He wanted to sit on the curb and cry.
Then he remembered a line on his fridge, from the Roman emperor Marcus Aurelius:
The impediment to action advances action. What stands in the way becomes the way.
So Hal walked a minute, ran a minute. The cramp became his plan.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE CROWD
segments.quote: If you are losing faith in human nature, go out and watch a marathon.
segments.author: Kathrine Switzer
lines: The last miles, strangers held out orange slices and signs that said, Touch here for power. He touched every one.
Nicole had read him a line from Kathrine Switzer, the first woman to run Boston with a race number:
If you are losing faith in human nature, go out and watch a marathon.
Hal finished in five hours and fifty-eight minutes. Next September, he stood at mile twenty with a bag of oranges.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Sign up. Walk first. Run ugly. Find your crew. Use the wall. Give back.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Sign up. Walk first. Run ugly. Find your crew. Use the wall. Then give back.
Me? I run only when the ice cream truck is leaving.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
